title: Kumrat Waterfall
subtitle: Roadside fall in the Kumrat valley, Upper Dir

landmark.name: Kumrat Waterfall
edits: The fall is drawn on the real slope: no terrace is cut (terrace 0). Trees within 100 m of the fall are left out so it can be seen (WorldCover 2021 maps tree cover there). The stream line runs from a lip at DEM 2520 m down to a plunge pool at the foot (DEM 2400 m), about 210 m long and about 120 m of drop measured from the Copernicus DEM (30 m DSM, approximate; the DSM smooths the chute and cannot show a lip, so the drop is an estimate and may be too large or small).

The gully is the DEM steepest-descent line through the slope above the valley floor. No stream is mapped in OSM here (the only mapped waterway in the box is the Panjkora River, about 200 m west), so the stream is not named and its line is not a surveyed one.

The gorge walls (two rows of displaced low-poly rock blocks, 8-15 m tall, about 7 m apart, grey with lichen-green patches), the foam (four steps of translucent sheets with scrolling streaks), the spray at each step and at the pool, the plunge pool (a flat disc about 16 m across) and the 10-20 boulders of 1-3 m at the foot are illustrative paint.
The OSM waterfall node (waterway=waterfall, id 6534025186) is at 35.569517, 72.192008, 0.1 m from the place point, and is used as the landmark point.
The drive is the Kumrat valley road (OSM tertiary, ref S-16); the trailhead is its nearest mapped vertex to the fall, about 180 m away. The walk to the foot (about 110 m) is traced over the DEM.
